bib.title: RAG VS FINE-TUNING: PIPELINES, TRADEOFFS, AND A CASE STUDY ON AGRICULTURE

question: What are the tradeoffs between RAG and fine-tuning for adding proprietary domain knowledge to LLMs, tested on a pipeline and an agriculture case study?
contributions: Comprehensive evaluation of LLMs (Llama2-13B, GPT-4, Vicuna) on agriculture questions with the full fine-tuning and RAG pipeline
Impact of retrieval and fine-tuning on LLM performance
Implications for other industries; a Q&A generation pipeline and metrics for question and answer quality

method.summary: Pipeline: scrape PDFs, extract structure with GROBID, generate 5 to 15 questions per section with Guidance, answer with Llama2-13B-chat+RAG (FAISS), fine-tune Llama2 models and GPT-4 (LoRA) on the Q&A, then compare base/fine-tuned models with and without RAG on 273 curated Washington questions graded by GPT-4.
method.task: domain question answering (agriculture), RAG vs fine-tuning

datasets.name: US agriculture documents
datasets.size: more than 23k PDF files, over 50M tokens, 44 states
datasets.split: Washington state subset of 573 files, over 2M tokens used for benchmark and fine-tuning
datasets.source: USDA, state agencies, Land-Grant Institutions National Program (public)
datasets.preprocessing: GROBID to TEI to JSON preserving sections, tables, captions

datasets.name: WA evaluation set
datasets.preprocessing: Section 4.3 says approximately 270 Q&A pairs generated by GPT-4 as ground truth; Section 5.3 says 273 human-curated

datasets.name: KVK farmer queries and Vikaspedia
datasets.size: 100,000 farmer queries from 27 Indian states, 2015 to 2022
datasets.preprocessing: Azure translation to English; Vikaspedia used to enrich answers

datasets.name: Knowledge-discovery questions
datasets.size: 1000 questions similar across at least three US states

other.also: fine-tuned with LoRA; also the judge, prompted five times per evaluation
generated the fine-tuning answers with RAG

other.also_trained: Open-Llama-3b and Llama2-7b, results not reported

other.use: Q&A generation quality study and metric calculation

training.objective: predict answer tokens given question prompt, prompt tokens masked (Llama2 models); LoRA on attention modules (GPT-4)
training.optimizer: Adam (Kingma and Ba; Loshchilov and Hutter cited)
training.lr: 2e-5 base (Llama2); 1e-4 base decayed during training (GPT-4 LoRA)
training.batch_size: 128 effective (microbatch 4 x 4 accumulation, 8 GPUs) for Llama2; 256 for GPT-4
training.hardware: Llama2: 8 H100 with PyTorch FSDP and activation checkpointing; GPT-4: seven nodes x 8 A100

other.framework: FastChat training script with flash-attention monkeypatching
other.train_set_size: number of Q&A pairs not stated

inference.samples: GPT-4 judge prompted 5 times per evaluation to measure variance; accuracy reported with +/- intervals, interval type not stated
inference.prompting: custom prompt with retrieved chunks as context to GPT-4 (text not given)
inference.retrieval: sentence-transformer embeddings, FAISS similarity_search_with_score, top-k=3; chunk size and embedding model not stated

parameters.BM25_and_dense: mentioned as options, FAISS dense used

metrics.name: Accuracy (Evaluation with Guideline)
metrics.definition: GPT-4 writes a guideline per ground-truth pair, then scores each answer 0 to 1 against it

metrics.name: Succinctness
metrics.definition: GPT-4 grades 1 (verbose) to 5 (succinct) with a scoring sheet

metrics.name: Correctness
metrics.definition: GPT-4 grades correct, partially correct, incorrect with a scoring sheet; reported as % fully correct

metrics.name: Recall@k
metrics.definition: how often the original source excerpt is retrieved for its generated question

metrics.name: Question metrics: Relevance, Global Relevance, Coverage, Fluency (1-5, LLM), Overlap (KL divergence), Diversity (WMD), Details (token count)

eval.protocol: GPT-4 as automatic judge, no human validation reported; accuracy intervals shown but their definition is not stated; no seeds

prompts.text: Answer the following questions with a single Yes or No: 1. The text mentions a specific location (City/State/Country), yes or no? ... If the text mentioned a location or locations, list them:
You are an expert in agriculture and you are formulating questions from documents to assess the knowledge of a student about agriculture-related topics.
Your task is to rate from 1 to 5 if the answer can be extracted from the context and the question

evidence.quote: The evaluation dataset is composed of 273 human-curated for the state of Washington.
GPT-4 was used to generate approximately 270 question and answer pairs from the agriculture documents as the ground truth dataset.

results.claim: Fine-tuning GPT-4 (LoRA) raised guideline accuracy from 75% to 81% on the WA benchmark.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks
results.table: Table 18, row GPT-4 (Fine-tuned), column Accuracy (81%±5%) vs row GPT-4 column Accuracy (75% ±3%)

results.claim: RAG on top of the fine-tuned GPT-4 gives 86% accuracy, cumulative with fine-tuning.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks
results.quote: GPT-4 displayed exceptional performance, securing an accuracy of 86% with RAG and 81% without RAG.

results.claim: Base GPT-4 gains 5 points from RAG (75% to 80%); the abstract states the fine-tuning (+6 p.p.) and RAG (+5 p.p.) gains are cumulative.
results.setup: Same WA benchmark; base GPT-4 without and with RAG
results.note: Intervals: 75% ±3%, 80% ±4%, 81%±5%, 86% ±2% so the steps are within about one interval of each other.
results.quote: We see an accuracy increase of over 6 p.p. when fine-tuning the model and this is cumulative with RAG, which increases accuracy by 5 p.p. further.

results.claim: Fine-tuning Llama2-13B (base completion model) on the generated Q&A scored 68%, below the off-the-shelf Llama-2-chat 13B at 76%.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks; Llama2 13B fine-tuned with LR 2e-5, 4 epochs; no un-tuned Llama2-13B base row in the table
results.table: Table 18, row Llama2 13B (Fine-tuned), column Accuracy (68% ±3%) vs row Llama-2-chat 13B (76% ±2%)

results.claim: RAG did not help Llama-2-chat 13B on accuracy (76% to 75%) but helped Vicuna (72% to 79%) and Llama2 13B fine-tuned (68% to 77%).
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks
results.table: Table 18, row Llama-2-chat 13B, columns Accuracy and +RAG (76% ±2%, 75% ±2%)

results.claim: RAG raised the share of fully correct GPT-4 answers from 36% to 60%; fine-tuned GPT-4 reached 45% and 61% with RAG.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks; fully correct as judged by GPT-4 with scoring sheet
results.table: Table 20, row GPT-4, columns Fully correct (%) and +RAG (36%, 60%); row GPT-4 Fine-tuned (45%, 61%)

results.claim: Vicuna had the largest gain in fully correct answers from RAG, 28% to 56%.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks
results.quote: We see the biggest improvement for Vicuna with the addition of RAG, going from 28% to 56% fully correct.

results.claim: RAG makes answers more succinct; GPT-4+RAG scores 3.2 of 5, but fine-tuned GPT-4+RAG stays at 2.5.
results.setup: 273 human-curated Washington-state questions with evaluation guidelines; GPT-4 judge scores each answer 0 to 1 against a guideline; Q&A for fine-tuning generated by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG over 573 WA documents (about 2M tokens); RAG uses top-3 FAISS chunks; succinctness 1 (verbose) to 5 (succinct), GPT-4 judge with scoring sheet
results.quote: GPT-4+RAG tends to provide the most succinct responses, with a score of 3.2 out of 5, though we do not see this improvement with fine-tuned GPT-4+RAG.

results.claim: In a cross-state knowledge test (1000 questions similar across at least three states, removed from training) base GPT-4 answered 47% 'similar' to reference, fine-tuned 72%, fine-tuned+RAG 74%.
results.setup: 1000 questions across US states, cosine similarity of embeddings; similarity of answer to reference graded Similar / Somewhat similar / Not similar; GPT-4 base vs fine-tuned vs fine-tuned+RAG; judge not stated for this table
results.note: Table 22 caption reads 'Accuracy of the base models and the fine-tuned models with and without RAG' but the rows are similarity categories. Text describes 72% and 74% as an 'upper bound' of what could be learned. Abstract: increasing answer similarity from 47% to 72%.
results.quote: GPT-4 was only able to learn 47% of the new knowledge presented to it.

results.claim: Retrieval recall of the source passage at top-3 is 81.5% over the 573 WA documents; top-1 61.9%, top-10 93.6%.
results.setup: Questions generated from 573 WA documents; recall = original excerpt retrieved for the question; FAISS index of sentence-transformer embeddings
results.table: Table 16, row 3, column Recall (81.5%); row 1 (61.9%); row 10 (93.6%)

results.claim: Recall@3 falls from 81.5% to 75.0% as the index grows sixfold (573 to 3888 documents).
results.setup: Index rebuilt with documents from other states; recall@3 measured on WA benchmark
results.quote: Despite that, the relevant context is retrieved more than 75% of cases even when the index increases sixfold (from 573 to 3888 documents).

results.claim: The paper's own summary of tradeoffs: RAG has low initial cost but larger prompts and more verbose, harder-to-steer output; fine-tuning has high initial cost, precise brevity-tuned output and minimal input tokens.
results.setup: Qualitative table from the GPT-4/Llama study in agriculture
results.note: Table 23 gives 'New Knowledge' as 'If data is in context' for RAG and 'New skill in domain' for fine-tuning.
results.table: Table 23, rows Initial cost, Cost - input token size, Cost - output token size, New Knowledge

results.claim: GPT-4 fine-tuning cost 1.5 days on seven nodes of eight A100 GPUs.
results.setup: LoRA fine-tuning of GPT-4, 4 epochs, batch 256, LR 1e-4
results.quote: The fine-tuning was carried out on seven nodes, each with eight A100 GPUs, over a total runtime of 1.5 days.

results.claim: Collected US data is more than 23k PDFs with over 50M tokens across 44 states; the WA benchmark subset is 573 files with over 2M tokens.
results.setup: USDA, state agencies and Land-Grant partners
results.quote: Collected data totals more than 23k PDF files with over 50M tokens, representing 44 states in the USA.

results.claim: Combined Q&A generation vs questions only: only-questions gives higher coverage (4.34 vs 3.97, no context) and better diversity; combined gives higher relevance (4.80 vs 4.12).
results.setup: Questions generated with GPT-4, metrics computed with GPT-3.5, WA documents
results.table: Table 15, rows Combined generation / Only questions, No context, columns Coverage, Relevance

limits: Single domain (agriculture) and single benchmark region (Washington state); fine-tuning and RAG data come from the same 573 documents.
Judge is GPT-4 for all accuracy figures, with no human agreement check; intervals are wide (+/-2 to 5%) and their definition is not stated.
Fine-tuning training data are answers written by Llama2-13B-chat with RAG, so fine-tuned models learn from a weaker teacher.
Evaluation-set origin is stated two ways (approximately 270 GPT-4-generated vs 273 human-curated).
Fine-tuned Llama2-13B is compared with instruction-tuned chat models, not with its un-tuned base.
Knowledge-discovery Table 22 mislabelled as accuracy and judge unspecified; Llama2-7b and Open-Llama-3b training mentioned but not reported.
Code, data and LoRA rank not released or stated.
Authors concede GPT-4 fine-tuning and inference cost must be weighed, and defer analysis of what knowledge the fine-tuned model gains to future work.
